summary.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
summary.one_liner: A book that compares the fundamental ideas, trade-offs and limitations behind data storage and processing systems so you can choose and reason about them.
keywords: data storage and processing tools comparison
takeaways: Compare the fundamental ideas and trade-offs across a broad range of data storage and processing systems
Understand the trade-offs and fundamental limitations that data systems face, rather than configuration details of one tool
Judge academic data systems ideas by how they perform in practice under intensive workloads
Learn why systems were designed the way they are, not just how they work
summary.summary: This is the landing page for Martin Kleppmann's book Designing Data-Intensive Applications. It presents the book as a guide to the trade-offs behind data storage and processing tools, covering concepts such as NoSQL, scalability, the CAP theorem, eventual consistency and sharding. The page says it focuses on fundamental ideas rather than how to configure specific tools, and ties academic research back to practical, real-world usage. It also includes endorsements and author background, which are not factual content about the book's topics.
